thread:
olivia: Quick follow-up from the RFC thread — I sketched an implementation called the attr-compression adapter. Want a short sync and to capture migration constraints.

sam: sgtm to sync. can you paste the sketch here?

olivia: short version: adapter runs in ingest path, canonicalizes attribute keys, applies lossless compression for dense payloads, and exposes two outputs: compact-envelope (primary) + retention-attr (sparse fallback). Idea is to avoid full envelope cloning in downstream consumers.

jamal: is this a binary transform or a proto evolution? curious about backwards compatibility with older analyzers.

olivia: proto-compatible. the adapter writes a compressed blob into an optional field `compressed_attrs_v1` and keeps a tiny header with a schema id + fingerprint. Consumers can opt-in to expand. legacy consumers continue reading the root attributes as-is (we keep a small uncompressed prefix).

anya: how do we handle cost attribution? our billing pipeline expects explicit tokenized attributes for bucketing. compression can't hide keys we need for cost.

olivia: agree — the header will include a deterministic sampling / billing-key projection that replicates the minimal set of attributes used by billing. That projection is always written uncompressed. so attribution stays intact.

sam: would that increase envelope size for typical traces? worst-case we add both projection + compressed blob.

olivia: yes in the short run. but we plan an adaptive strategy: only compress when attribute payload delta > threshold (e.g., > 1.5x typical attr size). heuristics in adapter. default behavior: no-op for tiny envelopes.

jamal: migration concerns: what about late enrichment? some enrichers add keys post-ingest today. If compaction happens earlier, they need to operate against expanded attrs or an API to mutate compressed blob.

olivia: plan A: move compaction as late as possible (post-enrich stage) but before fanout. Plan B: provide an expand/merge shim in the enrichment layer. shim exposes `expand_for_enricher()` that lazily materializes attrs.

anya: expand_for_enricher sounds fine but could blow CPU. have numbers?

olivia: rough bench: expand ~ 0.5ms per envelope on x86 alloc-heavy path. With batching and reuse it's ~0.2ms avg. We can mitigate via pool + arena alloc and by skipping expand when enricher touches only header attrs.

sam: ok. ops questions: who owns the adapter? runtime infra or eng-platform?

olivia: proposal: eng-platform owns the adapter logic + config; runtime infra owns the hotpath performance work and C++/Rust kernel.

jamal: can we keep a toggle per-tenant for safety? need rollback on perf regressions.

olivia: yes — per-tenant feature flag + global kill-switch in console. rollout plan uses canary tenants ~ 1% then ramp. metrics to watch: envelope size, ingest p95 latency, enrich CPU, billing mismatch delta.

anya: tests: need deterministic golden files for decompress and cost-key projection. also end-to-end query correctness tests (attribution queries must match pre-migration).

olivia: added to checklist: unit tests for serializer, property tests for roundtrip, integration test comparing billing buckets before/after on samplestore.

infra-bot: deploy-check triggered for branch `attr-compress/adapt-refactor` — CI: 38/42 passed, 4 flaky failures in `enricher_integration_test`.

sam: flaky tests first. jamal can you look into enricher_integration_test flakes? might be due to race on expand API.

jamal: on it. probable race between async expand and enrichment RPC. will push a fix to ensure expand completes before enricher starts.

olivia: design question: do we expose an API to query compressed schema ids so downstream analytics can choose to pull expanded attrs lazily?

anya: yes please. analytics jobs may want to offline expand only for a subset. expose `schema_id` + a stable fingerprint so backfills can fetch only matching envelopes. saving IO for backfills.

sam: data retention/regulatory: compressed blob content must still be subject to redaction rules. how do we redact inside compressed data?

olivia: redact before compressing. the adapter will run redaction hooks identical to current enricher pipeline to ensure PII never lands inside compressed field. we keep audit logs of redaction runs.

jamal: ops fallback: if adapter fails, we should fallback to passthrough envelope (no compression) and emit a metric. don't drop data.

olivia: agreed — fail-open. also increment an `adapter_error` counter with tenant tag and sample blown-up envelopes to internal blobstore for postmortem.

anya: curious about storage savings estimate. do we have sample corpus results?

olivia: yes ran on last week sample (1M envelopes): median attr size 1.2KB -> compressed median 0.4KB for dense cases; net system-wide predicted saving ~18% of trace storage and ~12% ingest egress after accounting for header. big wins on high-cardinality services.

sam: that's helpful. any query perf regressions: compressed blobs mean some queries that scan attrs can't index. how do we keep query shape?

olivia: indexing relies on the projection keys. We intentionally keep all keys used in queries that power SLOs & billing uncompressed. For ad-hoc analytics that need full attrs, we rely on on-demand expansion in worker clusters or pre-warm expansion for hot partitions.

jamal: what about observability of the adapter itself? tracing, SLI, and sampling?

olivia: adapter adds its own trace span with attribute counts and schema_id. SLIs: error rate < 0.01%, p99 add < 5ms, CPU budget tracked in infra console.

anya: final ask from product: a short blurb for the console UI to explain compressed envelopes to customers and the opt-out process.

olivia: will draft a customer note and a short FAQ. adding action items now.

olivia: Action items: 1) jamal: fix expand race + push CI. 2) olivia: PR w/ proto change + serializer + unit tests. 3) sam: create canary tenant list + rollout playbook. 4) anya: ops integration tests for billing parity. 5) all: review perf numbers Wed 11am.

sam: thanks — let's keep sync tight. :thumbsup:
